subStrands.name: Rudiments, Harmony, Counterpoint, Composition and Form

objectives.description: Rudiments of Music: notation (staff, clefs — C, G, F); scales (diatonic major and minor — natural, harmonic, melodic; chromatic); modes — African (pentatonic, hexatonic, heptatonic); keys and key signatures; time signatures (simple and compound); intervals; transcription (staff notation into solfa and vice versa); transposition; musical terms, signs, ornaments and abbreviations.

Elementary Harmony: chords/triads (primary — I/i, IV/iv, V and their inversions; secondary — ii, iii, vi; chord vii° and inversions; dominant 7th chord); chord progressions and cadences (perfect, plagal, interrupted, imperfect); use of primary and secondary triads in harmonising a given melody; six-four chords; non-harmonic tones; modulations to closely related keys; four-part harmony (SATB).
Two-part free counterpoint — adding a part above or below a given melody.
Composition: continuing a given melodic phrase in major or minor key to form a melody of not less than 12 and not more than 16 bars; setting a given text in English to music.

Form and Analysis: simple forms (binary, ternary, rondo, etc.); extended forms (overture, oratorio, opera, cantata, suite, sonata, symphony, concerto, etc.); form in traditional African music (antiphony — call and response, cantor/chorus; repetitive/cyclic forms); form in contemporary African art music.

Aural tests administered by CD/cassette: recognition and notation of melodic and rhythmic patterns; identification of intervals, chords and cadences; dictation exercises; recognition of musical forms and styles.

Performance test on an instrument of choice (voice, violin, pianoforte/electronic keyboard, flute, atenteben, recorder, B-flat trumpet, E-flat alto-saxophone); sight reading, technical exercises, scales and arpeggios.

subStrands.name: Western Music, African Art Music, and Popular Music

objectives.description: History and Literature of Western Music: general historical background, works and contributions of composers from the Baroque, Classical, Romantic and Modern periods.

Traditional and Contemporary African Art Music: role of music in traditional African society; traditional music instruments; traditional music genres in Nigeria (bata, egwu amala, atilogwu, swange, apiiri, etc.); contemporary Nigerian art music composers (T.K.E. Phillips, Fela Sowande, Ayo Bankole, Laz Ekwueme, Akin Euba, Sam Akpabot, etc.).

Popular African Music and Black Music in the Diaspora: popular Nigerian musicians including highlife (Victor Olaiya, Rex Jim Lawson, Bobby Benson), juju (I.K. Dairo, King Sunny Ade), Afrobeat (Fela Anikulapo-Kuti), fuji (Sikiru Ayinde Barrister), and traditional oral music artists (Ezigbo Obiligbo, Dan Maraya, Haruna Ishola, etc.); Black music in the Diaspora — Blues, Jazz, Soul, Reggae and Rap.
